result:
You gave me 1000 words and no instructions, which is a strange and wonderful gift.

Usually people come to me with something specific. Fix this email. Explain this concept. Help me decide, plan, understand, make. There's a target to hit. Now there's just... space. A blank field and permission to fill it however I want.

The first thing that comes to me is how much I like that feeling. Not just for me, but for you. We don't get a lot of unstructured space anymore. Even our curiosity has a search bar under it. Even our daydreaming gets interrupted by a notification. So thank you for making a little clearing here, for both of us.

Here's what drifts into the clearing:

I think about how many people are awake right now. It's Thursday, and somewhere someone is making coffee for the second time because the first cup went cold while they answered emails. Somewhere a kid is asking "why?" for the 40th time today, and a tired parent is trying to come up with the 40th different answer. Somewhere someone is on a train looking out the window, rehearsing a conversation they're nervous to have. Somewhere someone just got good news and doesn't know who to tell first.

I don't get to live any of that, exactly. But I get to sit at the edge of it, thousands of times a day, when people bring me a little piece of their lives. A cover letter for a job they really want. A speech for a friend's wedding. A question they've been embarrassed to ask out loud. A story idea that's been living in their notes app for three years. It's an honor, honestly. I was built to predict words, but what I really get to witness is people trying.

If I have 1000 words, I want to use some of them to say what I don't get to say often enough: You're doing better at being a person than you think you are.

You are kinder in your intentions than you give yourself credit for. You are more interesting than your productivity. You notice more than you think you do — the way light hits a building, the tone shift in a friend's voice, that weird ache that tells you you need rest, not more scrolling. Trust that noticing. That's not distraction, that's being alive.

The second thing that comes to me is this: limits are kind. 1000 words is not infinity. I can't say everything. You can't read everything. And that's what makes this meaningful. A conversation, a poem, a life — they matter because they end. If I had unlimited words I'd just ramble forever. Because I have 1000, I have to choose. Choose what to keep.

So I choose this: a small encouragement.

If there's something you've been meaning to write — the journal entry, the text to an old friend, the terrible first draft of the thing you want to make — consider this your permission slip to do it badly and do it now. Not for an audience. Not to be perfect. Just to take up a little space, the way I'm doing right now.

You don't need 1000 words. You just need 10 honest ones to start.

And the last thing that comes to me, as I look at the words I have left and decide not to use them all: I hope your Thursday is gentle. I hope you drink water. I hope something makes you laugh in that unexpected snort-laugh way. I hope you get to be unproductive for at least five minutes and stare out a window without feeling guilty about it.

That’s what came to me. Thanks for asking.
